2027-04-15.title: Thursday after the Second Sunday after Qyomtho
readings: A priest through the power of an indestructible life
Strive to enter through the narrow door
2027-04-15.alt: Season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection), the week after the Second Sunday after the Resurrection. The Letter to the Hebrews is read on most weekdays of these weeks.
2027-04-15.verse: One who has become a priest, not through a legal requirement concerning physical descent, but through the power of an indestructible life.
theo: Christ is risen! In these weeks of Qyomtho our Church reads the Letter to the Hebrews almost every weekday, and today it asks a bold question. Israel had a priesthood given by God himself: the sons of Aaron, from the tribe of Levi, served at the altar, and “the people received the law under this priesthood.” Why, then, did the Scriptures speak of “another priest arising according to the order of Melchizedek”? Jesus was not a Levite; “it is evident that our Lord was descended from Judah.” His priesthood does not rest on a family tree. He became a priest “not through a legal requirement concerning physical descent, but through the power of an indestructible life.” This is an Easter sentence. The life that the Cross could not end and the tomb could not hold is the very foundation of his priesthood. The Letter does not despise the priesthood of Aaron; that priesthood was God's gift and a preparation, and the Church sees in it a figure of what Christ fulfils (Catechism 1539–1545). St John Chrysostom, preaching on this chapter, observes that a priest who dies needs a successor, but the priest who lives for ever needs none (in substance).

The Gospel finds Jesus on the road, “teaching as he made his way to Jerusalem.” Someone asks, “Lord, will only a few be saved?” Jesus does not give a number. He turns the question from curiosity to decision: “Strive to enter through the narrow door.” A day comes when the owner of the house has shut the door, and some will knock and say, “We ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets.” Having been near him is not yet the same as having entered by him. The warning is not for one people; it is for every believer who thinks that knowing the Lord's name or sitting at his table is a guarantee without a changed life, and so it speaks first to us who receive the Holy Qurbono. Christian writers have said that the door is narrow only for the proud; for the humble it is wide enough. Then comes the great hope of the passage: “people will come from east and west, from north and south, and will eat in the kingdom of God.” We are among those who came from the east. The faith reached our shores through the preaching of the apostle Mar Thoma, as our tradition holds, and now we too are called to the banquet.

How do we live this today? The priest who lives for ever is the priest of every Holy Qurbono. When the celebrant stands at the altar of our church, it is Christ, risen and alive, who offers and who gives himself; “he always lives to make intercession” for us (Hebrews 7:25). The “better hope, through which we approach God” is not an idea but a person. So come to the Holy Qurbono this Easter season with the readiness of one who enters a door, not only of one who watches from the street. Pray today for the priests of our eparchy and for those preparing for the priesthood, that they may serve as men who belong to the eternal priest. And choose the narrow door in small things: one honest word, one act of forgiveness, one confession made before the coming Sunday. The door is narrow because it is the shape of Christ himself, and through him the way is open to all.
outline: Ask: am I standing at the door, or have I entered?
Point 1 · A priest who cannot die
His priesthood rests on the power of an indestructible life.
Nearness is not yet entrance; humility makes the door wide.
The banquet of the kingdom, and our place in it.
“Through the power of an indestructible life.”
live: Before the Holy Qurbono this week, spend a minute in silence asking Christ the High Priest to bring you to the Father.
Choose one hard but right thing you have been postponing, and do it before Sunday.
2027-04-15.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, you became our high priest through the power of an indestructible life. You live for ever to make intercession for us. Bring us through the narrow door of humility, that we may not only eat and drink in your presence but truly belong to you. Gather your children from east and west, from north and south, to the table of your kingdom, and keep our priests faithful to you. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: At every Holy Qurbono the living Christ, priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek, offers himself and gives us his Body and Blood, the bread and wine of the new and eternal covenant.

quick: Jesus is priest not by descent but through the power of an indestructible life: his priesthood rests on his Resurrection.
Being near the Lord is not enough; we must strive to enter through the narrow door.
People will come from east and west to eat in the kingdom of God, and we are among them.
2027-04-15.action: Pray today for one priest by name.
2027-04-15.question: Am I content to stand near Jesus, or am I striving to enter through the door?

family.explain: Someone asked Jesus how many people would be saved. Jesus did not give a number. He said: try hard to go in through the narrow door. A narrow door is one we pass through by bending low and leaving our big bags of pride outside. Jesus also said that people from every side of the world will come and sit at God's great feast. Our family is invited too.
family.intention: We pray for our parish priest and for all who will become priests.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing we can leave outside so that we can go through God's door?”

illus: In an old house near Kuravilangad the front door was so low that every visitor had to bend to enter. A grandson, tall at fifteen, struck his head on it one Easter holiday and complained. His grandfather laughed and said, “The man who built this house wanted every guest to bow a little before coming in. Even I bow, every day.” Years later the boy, by then a young engineer, told the story in a parish youth meeting on the Gospel of the narrow door: “The door was not too small. I was standing too straight.”

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, our high priest who lives for ever, we gather in your name. Open the door of your word to us tonight. Amen.
share: Not through a legal requirement concerning physical descent, but through the power of an indestructible life (Hebrews 7:16). What does it mean for me that my high priest is alive?
Strive to enter through the narrow door (Luke 13:24). Where is the narrow door in my life this week?
People will come from east and west, from north and south (Luke 13:29). How can our group welcome people who feel far from God?
interc: For the Church in this season of Qyomtho, that she may welcome all peoples to the table of the kingdom.
For our bishops and priests, that they may serve as men who belong to the eternal priest.
For young men discerning a call to the priesthood.
For those who once ate and drank in the Lord's presence and have drifted away, that they may return.
For all who feel unworthy to approach God, that they may know the door is open to the humble.
pm.close: Father, you made your risen Son our high priest for ever. Through him we approach you with a better hope. Make us humble enough to enter by the narrow door, and gather us with your saints at the banquet of your kingdom. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today the Letter to the Hebrews tells us that Jesus is not a priest because of the family he was born into. He became a priest through the power of an indestructible life (Hebrews 7:16).

That is the Easter mystery. The life that death could not destroy is the root of his priesthood. A priest who dies needs someone to take his place; our high priest lives for ever and always intercedes for us.

In the Gospel someone asks, “Lord, will only a few be saved?” Jesus answers: strive to enter through the narrow door (Luke 13:24). Some will say, “We ate and drank with you,” and still stand outside. Being near the Lord is not yet the same as entering by him. The door is narrow for the proud and wide for the humble.

And yet the promise is wide: people will come from east and west and eat in the kingdom of God. We have come from the east. Let us enter by the door who is Christ: in humble confession, in faithful coming to the Holy Qurbono, in daily love. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is alive, and he is our priest for ever! Someone asked him how many people would go to heaven. Jesus said: try hard to go in through the narrow door. To pass through a low, narrow door you have to bend down. That is what humble people do. Can you do one humble thing today, like saying sorry first or letting someone else go first?

intro: Theme: “Through the power of an indestructible life.”
On this Easter weekday: the priest who cannot die, the narrow door, and the banquet that gathers east and west.

sub: Not the order of Aaron, but of Melchizedek.
Not physical descent, but an indestructible life.
He always lives to intercede for us.
q: And King Melchizedek of Salem brought out bread and wine; he was priest of God Most High.
Consequently he is able for all time to save those who approach God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them.
points.apply: At the Holy Qurbono this week, entrust one person you love to the intercession of Christ the High Priest.

sub: “We ate and drank with you”: nearness is not yet entrance.
Narrow for the proud, wide for the humble.
q: This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous shall enter through it.
I am the gate. Whoever enters by me will be saved, and will come in and go out and find pasture.
points.apply: Do one humble act today that your pride has been resisting: an apology, a request for help, a confession.

sub: The table of the kingdom is wide.
We are among those who came from the east.
q: For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering.
I tell you, many will come from east and west and will eat with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.
points.apply: Invite one person who has stopped coming to church to the Holy Qurbono with you this Sunday.

concl: Our high priest is the risen Christ, who lives for ever and brings us to God.
The door is narrow because it is Christ himself; through him the way is open to all who come humbly.
2027-04-15.resolve: This week, enter by the narrow door in one concrete choice, and pray daily for priests.
